limitations: Concept-only review, not game integration, collision, native-grid, animation, physical safety or story-runtime validation.
Furniture and samples do not establish consent, actual payments, relocation, source disclosure or quest resolution.
Source appearance is not canon geography or a final identity/age model.

findings.finding: One detached notched worm-marked beam sits on two trestles. Stored saw is behind the work area; visitor path bypasses the sample and leads to the foreground lane. Quote pavilion has its own street approach and separated blank tablets. Background homes remain intact; no resident relocation or live support removal appears. These visual props cannot establish consent: every actual resident needs their own scoped choice; safe accommodation, acceptance, relocation and expenses must actually precede any approved occupied-beam removal. Buyer payment is not resident authorization. Extra stacked boards cannot become approved stock.

Old damaged section and separate smaller comparison disk are displayed; the visibly damaged standing tree is fenced off from the public bypass. Patrol hut opens to public lane and displays whistle, three pegs, closed folio and schematic forest routes without readable addresses or household names. This supports independent public access and limited route information; it does not certify tree diagnosis, all-forest disease, staffing, consent or erasure of historical address leakage.

High embankment path is visible and independent of the moored raft. Right storage shelter connects to a high dry public route beside an intact supported house; detached beams do not visibly come from a dismantled occupied roof. However, LEFT low weighing quay is separated from its high path by a retaining wall and continuous railing, with no visible dry stair/ramp connecting the two. Steps lead down to the raft/water, not up to the public path. An off-frame connection cannot be assumed. Add a visible dry return connection, preserving the high through-path and keeping refusal/flood closure independent of raft use, before using this as a resolved access layout. The raft is mostly unloaded and waterline marks are subtle; load capacity and actual approved material quantities are unknown. Refund token proves no refund or relocation.

overall: 90/91 support limited public inspection; 92 needs a visible low-quay to high-path dry return connection. Occupied-beam consent/relocation remains a required state check, not an art inference.
